decisions.reason: As a bread loaf close to the core bakery range, it is cheap to carry, fits existing craft and sourcing capabilities, and with only one year of market evidence its option value likely still exceeds the cost of keeping it.

The guided historic mill tour extends the firm's existing hospitality and tour offer, but it likely needs more staff time and coordination than a baked good, so it is somewhat more droppable even though uncertainty about demand is still not fully resolved.

As a sweet pastry very near the established confectionery business, it can be produced and sold through existing channels at low incremental cost, making it sensible to retain while the firm learns more about its demand.
